summary: Vijayalakshmi Mani is a scholar of Indology and history and archaeology. She studied as a Ph.D. scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi, attested in 2026.
Viktor Iosifovich Balin (1925–1991) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University from around 1946 to 1951, where he also taught in 1952.

Vilgelm Mikhailovich Berner (1903–1958) was an Indologist. He studied at the Leningrad Oriental Institute in 1931 and served as an aspirant at the Institute of Anthropology, Moscow State University, from 1935 to 1936.

Vilhelm Peter Grønbech (1873–1948) was a religious studies and linguistics scholar. He earned his cand.mag. at the University of Copenhagen, studying under Vilhelm Thomsen, Karl Verner, and Holger Pedersen, later teaching at Copenhagen and Danmarks Lærerhøjskole.

Vilhelm Thomsen (1842–1927) was a linguist and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied under Madvig and Westergaard at the University of Copenhagen, where he was later professor (1887–1913), and served as Chairman of the Royal Danish Academy.

Vilhelm Trenckner (1824–1891) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Johan Nicolai Madvig, Christian Thorning Engelstoft Hermansen, and Niels Ludvig Westergaard, later teaching at Det Kgl. Vajsenhus from 1860.

Ville Husgafvel is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He was a visiting research student at SOAS University of London and completed his doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki, where he worked as a project researcher (2022–2023).

Vimla Karnatak is an Indology and philosophy scholar. She studied under Gajanan Shastri Musalgaonkar and served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Banaras Hindu University, attested in 2000.

Vinay Lal (born 1961) is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Johns Hopkins University from around 1982 to 1984 and became a professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at UCLA around 1993.

Vinaya Kshirsagar is an Indologist and linguist. She was a professor at Dr. D. Y. Patil Medical College, Hospital & Research Centre in 2015 and is attested in 2026 as Professor-Editor of the Sanskrit Dictionary at Deccan College.

Vincenc Lesný (1882–1953) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Charles University, Oxford, and Bonn under Josef Zubatý, Moriz Winternitz, A. A. Macdonell, and Hermann Jacobi, later becoming professor at Charles University.

Vincenc Pořízka (1905–1982) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Palacký University Olomouc and Charles University under Vincenc Lesný and Otakar Pertold, later serving as Professor of Hindi at Charles University and holding a post at Humboldt University.

Vincent Arthur Smith (1848–1920) was an Indologist and historian. Educated at Trinity College Dublin and Cambridge, he served in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900) before working as Reader in Indian History at Dublin and Oxford, and Curator of Oxford's Indian Institute.

Vincent Breugem (born 1970) specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (MA, PhD), Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono Universities, as well as under Lucia Dolce, and served as a research fellow at Leiden University (attested 2012).

Vincent Eltschinger (born 1970) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He studied at Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, Fribourg, and Vienna. His posts include the Austrian Academy of Sciences, IKGA, and directeur d'études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Vincent Goossaert (born 1969) is a scholar of sinology and religious studies. He studied under Kristofer Schipper, worked at the CNRS from 1998 to 2012, and became Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2012.

Vincent Lefèvre is an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes, under Bruno Dagens, and at Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and has served as a curator at the Guimet Museum.

Vincent Tournier is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studied under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub and Seishi Karashima, and holds the Chair of Classical Indology at the University of Munich.

Vincenz Scherzl (1843–1906) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Charles University, King's College London, Saint Petersburg under Kaetan Kossovich, and Moscow State University. He served as professor of comparative linguistics at the universities of Kharkiv and Odesa.
Vincenzo Vergiani is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied under Raffaele Torella and was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Cambridge in 2007.
